cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested in hit-and-run that seriously injured 7-year-old boy
cards.teaser: Demetrius Johnson faces charges after allegedly striking a child in a crosswalk and driving away on Aug. 1.
cards.body:
The Fort Pierce Police Department arrested Demetrius Johnson in connection with an Aug. 1 hit-and-run crash that left a 7-year-old boy seriously injured. Johnson, 34, was arrested at 2905 U.S. Highway 1 and faces charges of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury and driving with a suspended license. The crash occurred at 8:55 p.m. at the intersection of North 25th Street and Avenue M.

Surveillance video from a nearby business shows two children running across the street in the crosswalk as a vehicle makes a sharp left turn and strikes the 7-year-old boy. Johnson is seen briefly getting out of his vehicle to check on the child before returning to the vehicle and driving away. Police say the 7-year-old boy has been released from the hospital and is recovering. The investigation remains ongoing.

hero.headline: 17 arrested in Indiantown cocaine trafficking ring, three remain wanted after months-long investigation
hero.body:
Seventeen people are in custody and three others remain wanted following a months-long narcotics investigation that authorities say dismantled a significant cocaine trafficking operation centered in Indiantown. The investigation, dubbed Operation Beneath the Surface, resulted in the seizure of four kilograms of cocaine, three ounces of methamphetamine, two pounds of marijuana and eight guns, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. Authorities said the defendants collectively face more than 200 felony charges.

The investigation began in late 2025 when narcotics detectives conducting undercover drug buys began dealing with Khalil Thompson and Christopher Wilson. Investigators said the two appeared to have a steady supply of cocaine, eventually leading detectives to Cecil Trimble of Indiantown, who authorities identified as the alleged leader of the operation. Investigators allege Trimble operated a car detailing business in Indiantown that served as a front for a much larger cocaine operation. The business inspired the name Operation Beneath the Surface, authorities said.

According to the sheriff's office, investigators obtained court-authorized wiretaps involving several of the suspected key players. Authorities said the investigation showed cocaine was being supplied to dealers in Indiantown, Stuart and Port St. Lucie, while other people were allegedly used as drug mules to transport cocaine to the Daytona Beach area. In one case, authorities said Antonio Honor was stopped by the Florida Highway Patrol while traveling north on Interstate 95 and was found with a kilogram of cocaine. Another woman, Chiquita Adamson, was also accused of transporting cocaine for the organization, though authorities said she was not caught with the drugs in her possession.

Investigators executed three residential search warrants, two in Indiantown and one in Stuart, as part of the operation. Authorities estimated the cocaine was being purchased at the kilogram level for about $20,000 each, while its potential street value could be substantially higher once divided for individual sales. The sheriff's office said the four kilograms of cocaine seized represent one of the most significant drug seizures investigators have made in the Booker Park area of Indiantown. Authorities said Trimble, Thompson, Wilson and Jamari Jones are among the defendants facing racketeering charges. Trimble was also on federal probation at the time of his arrest, according to the sheriff's office.

hero.headline: Rescued animals from Martin County hoarding cases begin showing signs of recovery
hero.teaser: More than 100 animals from two separate hoarding investigations in Stuart and Palm City are now at the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast in Palm City, where staff report many are already beginning to heal.
hero.body:
After Martin County authorities rescued 108 cats and dogs from a Stuart home on Southwest Meadowlark Circle owned by 77-year-old Gail Giustino and 36 Border Collies from a Palm City home where Paige O'Donnell was arrested, the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast in Palm City is now caring for over 100 animals. Cesar Perea, associate vice president of rescue for American Humane Society, said the emotional and physical recovery process for animals often begins quickly once they are removed from dangerous conditions.

The Border Collies rescued from the Palm City home are undergoing what shelter staff call medical grooming, a process that involves carefully shaving severely matted fur while checking for injuries and infections underneath. Sarah Fisher, spokesperson for the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, said staff shaved 9 pounds off of one dog filled with feces and urine. Some dogs arrived with metal and glass fragments trapped in their fur.

Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said in the Stuart case that investigators believed Giustino thought she was helping animals, despite the dangerous conditions inside the home. The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is currently encouraging the public to adopt or foster available animals while the rescued Border Collies continue receiving treatment. The shelter is also asking for donations to its emergency medical fund or through its Amazon Wish List.

WPTV previously reported that deputies found horrific conditions at Giustino's home on Southwest Meadowlark Circle in July, with no working air conditioning, little ventilation and up to a foot of animal feces covering the floor.The second case involved 36 Border Collies rescued from a Palm City home after deputies described severe neglect conditions. Paige O'Donnell was arrested and faces 72 criminal charges after WPTV's investigation helped renew the sheriff's office probe. Deputies found the dogs living in deplorable conditions, with fur matted with feces and debris.Cesar Perea, associate vice president of rescue for American Humane Society, said the emotional and physical recovery process for animals often begins quickly once they are removed from dangerous conditions."As soon as you start providing care, you immediately start to see the animal's personality come out," Perea said. "When they were in that situation, they were completely shut down."Perea said American Humane has been assisting the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast with shelter operations and veterinary support following the rescues.The Border Collies rescued from the Palm City home are undergoing what shelter staff call "medical grooming," a process that involves carefully shaving severely matted fur while checking for injuries and infections underneath. During the initial rescue, she said staff found "lots of pieces of metal — rusted metal, sharp metal — that have been stuck in their fur, along with shards of glass."Perea said trauma in rescued animals can appear as emotional shutdown, inactivity and fear, but he has seen dramatic turnarounds in many hoarding cases across the country."Within two weeks, you wouldn't even recognize that animal," Perea said. "They start getting a little more active and joyful. hero.headline: Man shot and killed at Fort Pierce mobile home park, ex-girlfriend says 5-year-old son now without father
hero.body:
A 37-year-old man was shot and killed Wednesday night inside a mobile home at the Seminole Mobile Home Park on Orange Avenue in Fort Pierce, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Naomi Pallarez, the victim's ex-girlfriend, said the shooting has left their 5-year-old son without a father.

The shooting happened inside trailer 51, where a 22-year-old man, his sister, and his girlfriend were present. The sheriff said the two men, who knew each other, had been arguing over text messages before the incident. The shooter allowed the victim to come inside, at which time he was attacked by being pushed and then punched in the stomach multiple times, according to Sheriff Richard R. The 22-year-old man then pulled out a gun and shot the victim once.

Pallarez expressed her heartbreak over the loss. "I am very much heartbroken, and now I am a single mom," she said. "We didn't even get to say goodbye, do anything. The father of my child's birthday is Saturday, and he's gone." Pallarez said her concern now is what to tell her son about his father's death. As of the latest update, no charges have been filed in the case. Deputies with the Sheriff's Office Patrol Operations Bureau and personnel from the St. Lucie County Fire District responded to the scene at approximately 9:11 p.m. Wednesday. The victim was transported to a local hospital, where he was later pronounced dead.

hero.headline: Indian River County school district plans to sell 10 properties including 4 older schools
hero.body:
The School District of Indian River County is looking to put around 10 properties on the market for potential buyers after consolidating multiple schools throughout the district. The properties include four older schools, older office buildings, and district-owned land spread across the county.

William Dodds, CFO of the School District of Indian River County, said the space is no longer needed after consolidating schools. Dodds said maintaining two buildings when operations can be done in one is not the best financial decision. Money made from the sale would go back to the district's capital budget to help keep buildings up, enhance facilities, and fund capital projects that would not be possible otherwise.

Ken Krasnow with Cushman and Wakefield, a real estate company working with the school district to sell the properties, said the buildings vary in condition and potential. Krasnow said some buildings, like Rosewood Magnet School, could be transformed into medical office space or quasi-flex space. Krasnow said larger schools and properties could be redeveloped with commercial and retail space along the front and residential in the back.

No decisions have been made yet. Dodds said the district is gauging interest from potential buyers before moving forward. The district will reexamine interest in the properties and whether they need to be sold around December or January. The school board will have final approval.

hero.headline: Florida retirement costs show $600,000 gap between Gulf Coast and Atlantic Coast
hero.body:
A retiree on Florida's Gulf Coast needs roughly $550,000 in invested assets to fund retirement versus $1.15 million for the same lifestyle on the state's Atlantic Coast, according to new numbers from the online website 24/7 Wall St. The $600,000 gap reflects differences in housing costs, insurance premiums, property taxes, and other living expenses between the two regions.

The report examined retirement factors including housing, insurance, food, utilities, transportation and healthcare. Austin Smith, a financial publisher at 24/7 Wall St., said the math was based on a three-bedroom home fairly close to the water. Moving to a place like Delray Beach or Stuart could increase annual living costs by as much as $20,000, driven almost entirely by wind and flood coverage and higher property taxes.

Property taxes are a significant issue in Florida, with voters deciding on a referendum this November to raise the homestead exemption and lower property tax bills. Opponents of the referendum say cutting property taxes will only lead to raising other fees and taxes to maintain public safety and local services. Smith said the dynamics in Florida, particularly around insurance and housing costs, have made retirement location a Gulf Coast versus Atlantic conversation.

Florida has long been a popular destination for retirees and snowbirds, but Smith said not everybody can make that southeastern move work financially. The report highlights growing regional disparities within the state as coastal property insurance costs and property values continue to diverge between the Gulf and Atlantic sides of Florida.

cards.headline: Martin County deputies stop $600,000 gold bar scam targeting senior citizen
cards.teaser: A Martin County senior citizen nearly lost $600,000 to a gold bar scam before deputies helped stop the transaction and recover the full amount.
cards.body:
A Martin County senior citizen nearly lost $600,000 to a gold bar scam, but with the help of deputies, the crisis was averted. The victim was contacted by a fraudster claiming to be from his financial institution and was told that his bank account had been compromised. The scammer then convinced the senior citizen that he needed to protect his money by backing it up with gold.

The victim was instructed to send $600,000 to a legitimate gold vendor. The scammer told the victim that the gold would then be picked up by a third-party driver and delivered to the bank. After going through with the transaction, the victim quickly realized something was not right and immediately went to his bank. The bank then recognized the situation as potential fraud and advised him to contact the sheriff's office.

The responding deputy spoke directly with the gold vendor and helped the victim stop the transaction from going through. The victim confirmed he received a full refund of his $600,000.

After going through with the transaction, the victim quickly realized something wasn’t right, and immediately went to his bank. The bank then recognized the situation as potential fraud and advised him to the sheriff's office. See also: Elderly woman accused of stealing nearly $2,000 worth of merchandise from Wellington Mall The responding deputy then spoke directly with the gold vendor and helped the victim stop the transaction from going through. MCSO says the victim confirmed he received a full refund of his $600,000.

cards.headline: Palm City home condemned after 36 Border Collies rescued in animal hoarding case
cards.teaser: Martin County authorities condemned a Palm City home on Wednesday after arresting Paige O'Donnell on 72 charges in connection with the hoarding of 36 Border Collies in what the Humane Society calls the worst case it has seen.
cards.body:
A Palm City home has been condemned after Paige O'Donnell was arrested on 72 charges in connection with the hoarding of 36 Border Collies in what the Humane Society calls the worst animal hoarding case it has ever seen. The Martin County Building Department posted a notice of condemnation to the gate of the home on Wednesday. The notice states occupancy is prohibited as the structure is unfit for human occupancy as defined by section 21.75.3, citing an unsanitary single-family residence.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office arrested O'Donnell on Monday following a lengthy investigation into animal welfare concerns at her residence. When deputies executed a search warrant, they discovered dogs covered in feces and urine living in a home with no functioning air conditioning and floors covered in waste and garbage. O'Donnell is currently being held at the Martin County Jail on a $270,000 bond and does not have an attorney.

hero.headline: 16-year-old dies after falling through roof of abandoned building in Sebastian
hero.body:
A 16-year-old girl died after falling through a hole in the roof of an abandoned four-story building in Sebastian on Saturday night, according to the Indian River County Sheriff's Office.

Deputies and fire rescue personnel responded to 9846 Riverside Preserve Drive in Sebastian at about 10:35 p.m. after receiving a 911 call reporting that the girl had fallen from a concrete structure and was critically injured. Deputies arrived and found a group of minors along with the critically injured teen on the second floor of the abandoned building. The investigation determined the group had been trespassing on the property and was on the roof when the teen fell through a hole in the roof, dropping approximately 29 feet to the floor below.

One of the minors in the group knew CPR and immediately began life-saving measures. The 16-year-old was flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where she died from her injuries a short time later. Detectives are actively investigating the teen's death, but said all evidence indicates this was an accident.

The Indian River County Sheriff's Office extends its deepest sympathies to the family during this difficult time. The sheriff's office also reminded the public, especially parents and teens, of the serious dangers posed by climbing on abandoned structures and the legal consequences of trespassing on privately owned property. The victim's name has not been released.

cards.headline: Indian River County deputy talks man off 17th Street Bridge after two-hour standoff
cards.teaser: Deputies in Indian River County safely took a man into custody after a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge early Tuesday morning.
cards.body:
Deputies in Indian River County safely took a man into custody after a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge early Tuesday morning. The incident began around 1 a.m. when deputies responded to a call from Port St. Lucie police about a man wanted for burglary. The man had reportedly called his mother and told her he wanted to kill himself.

Body camera footage showed the man sitting on a platform over the bridge railing, his feet dangling in the air. Traffic Deputy Edouard Gast, a member of the Indian River County Sheriff's Office Crisis Negotiation Team, worked to establish a connection with the man. At one point, the man appeared ready to jump.

The sheriff's office marine unit and fire rescue crews were stationed in the water below as a safety precaution. After two hours of negotiation, the man climbed back to the top of the bridge and shook the negotiator's hand. The man was taken into custody without incident.

You got a lot on your mind?” The man responded, “Yeah, I do, and I’m trying to think about it.” At one point, the man appeared ready to jump. hero.headline: Homeowner shoots, kills man who attacked him at St. Lucie County mobile home park; stand your ground case under review
hero.body:
A 37-year-old man died Wednesday night after a 22-year-old homeowner shot him inside a residence at Seminole Mobile Home Park in the 3300 block of Orange Avenue following a physical attack that stemmed from an ongoing dispute between the two men. St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said the men had exchanged threatening text messages and verbal arguments before the shooting occurred at 9:11 p.m. The man who was killed knocked on the door, was let inside, then immediately pushed the homeowner and punched him twice in the midsection. The homeowner backed away, pulled out a 9 mm semi-automatic pistol, and shot the man once in the chest.

The man who was shot was taken to a local hospital, where he died from his injuries. The homeowner's sister and girlfriend were inside the home at the time and gave statements that corroborated his account of the incident. Investigators executed a search warrant at the residence and recovered the handgun. The sheriff said the suspect had a criminal history including drug-related charges, resisting officer charges, domestic violence-related charges, and three felony convictions.

No charges have been filed against the homeowner. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is working with the State Attorney's Office to determine whether the shooting falls under Florida's stand your ground self-defense law. Del Toro said investigators worked nine hours at the scene, which was cleared shortly after 6 a.m. Thursday. The name of the man who was killed has not been released.

Investigators described the shooting as an isolated incident and said there is no immediate threat to the surrounding community. Del Toro urged anyone who receives threats and believes a situation could escalate to contact law enforcement before violence occurs. The sheriff's office is asking anyone with information about the shooting to call 772-462-3230 or submit anonymous tips through Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-TIPS.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce police arrest driver 11 days after hit-and-run crash fractured 8-year-old girl's femur
cards.teaser: Demetris Johnson, 34, was arrested Wednesday and charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury and driving with a suspended license. Surveillance video showed him checking on the girl before driving away from the intersection of 25th Street and Avenue M.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police arrested 34-year-old Demetris Johnson on Wednesday, 11 days after a hit-and-run crash left an 8-year-old girl with a fractured femur. The crash happened at 8:55 p.m. on Saturday, August 1, at the intersection of North 25th Street and Avenue M when a Mercedes-Benz making a left turn struck the girl as she and her brother were crossing the street in a marked crosswalk. Surveillance cameras from a nearby business captured Johnson exiting the vehicle to check on the girl before getting back into the car and driving away.

Johnson was located and arrested at 2905 U.S. Highway 1 and faces charges of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injuries and driving while his license was suspended. He refused to speak with investigators. The girl's mother, Lawrunda Robinson, said her daughter is using a wheelchair and will need a month in a cast before beginning physical therapy to learn to walk again. Johnson is being held at the St. Lucie County Jail.

Sean Smith, Officer Jason Vega, and Detective Sgt. on paid administrative leave as the Florida Department of Law Enforcement takes over a criminal investigation into two incidents involving political campaign signs near SW Airoso Boulevard.
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie Police Department placed three officers on paid administrative leave effective August 13 as part of investigations into two incidents involving political campaign signs near SW Airoso Boulevard last week. The officers placed on leave are Detective Sgt. Sean Smith, Officer Jason Vega, and Detective Sgt. Chief Leo Niemczyk reviewed the initial facts and timeline surrounding the incidents before requesting assistance from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement to ensure the investigation remains fair, impartial, and unbiased.

FDLE has agreed to take over the criminal investigation into the campaign sign incidents. The department stated the criminal investigation must be completed before the internal administrative investigation begins to ensure both processes are conducted independently and appropriately. Once the criminal investigation concludes, the internal administrative investigation will proceed in accordance with established procedures, applicable law, and the Florida Law Enforcement Officers' Bill of Rights. The Port St. Lucie Police Department stated it will not provide additional information or comment on matters being handled by FDLE.

hero.headline: 36 Border Collies rescued from Palm City hoarding case show signs of hope after days of care
hero.teaser: Days after being rescued from a home on Southwest Alligator Street in Palm City, 36 Border Collies are beginning to show signs of hope as shelter workers provide around-the-clock care and rehabilitation.
hero.body:
The 36 Border Collies rescued from a severe animal hoarding situation in Palm City are beginning to show signs of hope as shelter workers provide around-the-clock care. The dogs were removed from a home on Southwest Alligator Street where Martin County deputies reported finding deplorable living conditions, including feces, urine-soaked materials, and debris throughout the residence. Homeowner Paige O'Donnell was arrested and faces animal cruelty and improper confinement charges. All 36 dogs are now in the care of the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, where staff members have spent the past several days working to help them recover physically and emotionally.

Many of the dogs arrived severely matted, under-socialized, and frightened of human interaction. Since arriving at the shelter, the dogs have received vaccines, deworming treatments, medications and extensive grooming. Sarah Fisher, a Humane Society spokesperson, said one puppy's mats weighed three pounds, and she estimated the big dogs' mats weighed at least double that. The dogs range in age from puppies younger than four months old to adults believed to be as old as six years. Shelter workers say the younger dogs appear to be adjusting more quickly, while many of the older dogs remain fearful and withdrawn after what may have been years of neglect.

Community members have provided monetary support, supplies, and encouragement for staff caring for the rescued animals after photos of the dogs were shared online. The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast says its most urgent needs are wet dog food and monetary donations to support the ongoing care and rehabilitation of the rescued Border Collies. The shelter is also currently over capacity and is seeking foster families willing to temporarily care for other dogs and cats in its system. The dogs cannot be adopted while legal proceedings continue, but once the case is resolved, the animals will be spayed and neutered, continue rehabilitation, and eventually be placed in foster homes or adopted by families prepared to meet their needs.
hero.article_text: Just days after 36 Border Collies were rescued from what authorities described as a severe animal hoarding situation in Palm City , shelter workers say the dogs are beginning to show signs of hope. The dogs were removed from a home on Southwest Alligator Street where Martin County deputies reported finding deplorable living conditions, including feces, urine-soaked materials, and debris throughout the residence. Homeowner Paige O'Donnell was arrested and faces animal cruelty and improper confinement charges . Now, all 36 dogs are in the care of the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast, where staff members have spent the past several days working around the clock to help them recover physically and emotionally. "It's been completely insane. We've been working our tails off, no pun intended," said Humane Society spokesperson Sarah Fisher. According to Fisher, many of the dogs arrived severely matted, under-socialized, and frightened of human interaction. Since arriving at the shelter, the dogs have received vaccines, deworming treatments, medications and extensive grooming. Some of the grooming challenges have been staggering. "Yesterday we shaved one of the puppy's mats off, and it was three pounds just on the puppy," Fisher said. "So, you can imagine the big dogs are probably at least double that." The dogs range in age from puppies younger than four months old to adults believed to be as old as six years. Shelter workers say the younger dogs appear to be adjusting more quickly, while many of the older dogs remain fearful and withdrawn after what may have been years of neglect. "Overall, they're all very under-socialized and scared," Fisher said. Staff has only been able to work on 10 dogs so far due to their extreme conditions. See also: Animal Services responded to Palm City home roughly 20 times since 2020 Some dogs have required sedation for grooming and medical treatment. Others are beginning to slowly warm up to staff members. Fisher says every dog is progressing differently, but many still have a long road ahead. "They're going to take a lot of time to really come out of their shell," she said. The recovery effort comes just weeks after another large animal hoarding case in Martin County, leaving shelter staff emotionally exhausted but determined to continue helping animals in need. Still, Fisher says the community response has been overwhelming. After photos of the dogs were shared online, donations from across the Treasure Coast began pouring in. Community members have provided monetary support, supplies, and encouragement for staff caring for the rescued animals. "The amount of support is so heartwarming. I can't even believe it," Fisher said. "And our staff is so grateful." For now, the dogs cannot be adopted while legal proceedings continue. Once the case is resolved, the animals will be spayed and neutered, continue rehabilitation, and eventually be placed in foster homes or adopted by families prepared to meet their needs. That process could take weeks or even months. But despite the challenges ahead, shelter workers say they've already noticed a change in the dogs since they first arrived. "From yesterday to today, I think they realize that they're safe now," Fisher said. "And you can see just a small transformation, and it just brings everybody's spirits up. So, they haven't fully given up." If you'd like to help, the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast says its most urgent needs are wet dog food and monetary donations to support the ongoing care and rehabilitation of the rescued Border Collies. The shelter is also currently over capacity and is seeking foster families willing to temporarily care for other dogs and cats in its system, helping free up much-needed space as these animals recover. Fisher says the shelter also has a 'Name your price' adoption special until further notice. "We have a 'name your price' adoption special until further notice too. (12:31) So, it's a good time to adopt.

cards.headline: Humane Society of Treasure Coast strained after 36 Border Collies rescued in Palm City
cards.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast says the latest Palm City hoarding case is the worst animal neglect staff has ever seen, with teams overwhelmed by the amount of care and rehabilitation the 36 Border Collies will need.
cards.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is feeling the pressure after 36 Border Collies were rescued from a hoarding case in Palm City this week. Sarah Fisher with the Humane Society said the latest case is the worst animal neglect she has ever seen. Fisher told CBS12 News that teams at the Humane Society are overwhelmed by the amount of care and rehabilitation the Border Collies will need, but are prepared to provide the dogs with the medical care, attention and support they desperately need.

Fisher said it will be some time before the dogs are ready for adoption. Once they are ready to find their forever homes, the Humane Society plans to identify families with experience caring for Border Collies. The organization will also look for families who have plenty of patience, because the dogs will need extensive socialization, training and time to adjust to their new surroundings.

hero.headline: Byron Donalds leads Florida Republican gubernatorial primary with 49% as Aug. 18 vote nears
hero.body:
Florida's Republican gubernatorial primary stands at a decisive tilt five days before the Aug. 18 election, with U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds holding a commanding lead while Democrats appear near settling their nomination. A James Madison Institute survey released in August placed Donalds at 49 percent among likely Republican primary voters, followed by Lt. Gov. Jay Collins at 18 percent, former House Speaker Paul Renner at 8 percent and investor James Fishback at 4 percent. Twenty-one percent remained undecided.

Donalds, who secured President Donald Trump's endorsement, centered his closing message on affordability and promised to lower Florida property insurance costs through changes to the state's Catastrophe Fund, reinsurance system and home hardening programs. He called the property tax amendment headed to voters only a first step and argued that faster permitting could reduce housing and construction costs. Donalds told reporters he feels confident about his position but acknowledged the outcome remains in voters' hands.

Collins escalated his attacks in a lengthy virtual news conference, casting himself as a day-one ready Florida executive and Donalds as a Washington celebrity disconnected from working families. Collins proposed tighter insurance oversight, faster claims and storm permitting, expanded home hardening and the eventual elimination of property taxes on homesteaded homes. He called the Republican contest a two-person race and urged Renner, Fishback and other candidates without viable paths to rally behind him, though recent public polling consistently shows Donalds leading by wide margins. Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed Collins lieutenant governor in August 2025 but has not endorsed anyone in the race to succeed him.

On the Democratic side, former Republican congressman David Jolly held 47 percent in the latest JMI survey, with no other Democratic candidate topping 5 percent. His running mate Gwen Graham cast her ballot at Florida A&M University and described the ticket as centrist and moderate, with an agenda focused on housing affordability, education and healthcare access. Florida had nearly 3.33 million voters registered with no party affiliation as of July 31, while Republicans held a registration advantage of more than 1.5 million over Democrats. The latest JMI survey showed Donalds leading Jolly 45 to 38 percent in a potential general election matchup. The primary is Aug. 18, and the general election is Nov. 3.
hero.article_text: With five days remaining before Florida's primary, the candidates for governor are making their final sales — and the two parties are ending in very different places.Republicans are still fighting over their nominee. Byron Donalds is working to protect a commanding lead, while Lt. Jay Collins is escalating his attacks and trying to consolidate voters looking for an alternative. Democrats, meanwhile, appear close to settling their primary, allowing David Jolly and running mate Gwen Graham to begin making their case for November.Donalds, endorsed by President Donald Trump, sounded confident in an interview Thursday but stopped short of declaring the race over."You stay confident, you stay focused on what you're doing," Donalds said. "I think the fact that the other campaigns attack me every day kind of demonstrates that they, too, know where things are in this race."Recent polling supports that confidence. A James Madison Institute survey released in August placed Donalds at 49 percent among likely Republican primary voters, followed by Collins at 18 percent, former House Speaker Paul Renner at 8 percent and investor James Fishback at 4 percent. Twenty-one percent remained undecided.Donalds kept his closing message centered on affordability, blaming Democratic economic policies for inflation and promising to lower Florida property-insurance costs through changes to the state's Catastrophe Fund, reinsurance system and home-hardening programs. He also called the property-tax amendment headed to voters only a "first step" and argued that faster permitting could reduce housing and construction costs."We feel very good about where we stand today, but it's in the hands of the voters," Donalds said. "We'll see what happens Tuesday night."Collins is closing much more aggressively.During a lengthy virtual news conference, the former Green Beret cast himself as a "day-one ready" Florida executive and Donalds as a Washington celebrity disconnected from working families."I mow my own yard, I gassed up my own truck, I live the same Florida life that working families live because I'm one of the people," Collins said.He then added a more personal jab: "Byron, I don't think he probably mows his yard. My guess is he has a landscape architect."Collins' policy pitch included tighter insurance oversight, faster claims and storm permitting, expanded home hardening and the eventual elimination of property taxes on homesteaded homes. He also proposed broader sales-tax holidays for families and tradespeople, a permanent Second Amendment sales-tax holiday and a requirement that large data centers cover the utility costs associated with their operations.His campaign's central promise: "Life will get easier. We will be safer."Collins called the Republican contest a two-person race and urged Renner, Fishback and the remaining candidates without a viable path to rally behind him. That characterization, however, is not reflected in recent public polling, which consistently shows Donalds leading the field by wide margins.Gov. Ron DeSantis appointed Collins lieutenant governor in August 2025, giving Collins the executive experience he now emphasizes. DeSantis, however, has not endorsed anyone in the race to succeed him.Despite his attacks, Collins pledged to support the eventual Republican nominee if he loses Tuesday."Yes, I will support whoever the nominee is," Collins said. "And yes, I absolutely think all Republicans should step in and support whoever the nominee is."The Democratic race has far less suspense.Jolly, a former Republican congressman who later became a Democrat, held 47 percent in the latest JMI survey. No other Democratic candidate topped 5 percent. Six candidates remain on the Democratic ballot.His running mate, Gwen Graham, is already speaking directly to November.Graham, a former Democratic congresswoman and the daughter of former Gov. Bob Graham, cast her ballot Thursday at Florida A&M University. She chose the historically Black university to highlight voting rights, civil rights and youth participation.FAMU students helped launch the Tallahassee bus boycott in 1956 after Wilhelmina Jakes and Carrie Patterson were arrested for refusing to follow segregated seating rules."FAMU has had a long history of fighting for civil rights, fighting for voting rights," Graham said. "The students of FAMU have had a historical impact."While saying the campaign is taking nothing for granted, Graham made clear the Jolly-Graham ticket is already looking beyond Tuesday."It's a short sprint between Aug. "This race is not about being a Democrat, Republican or Independent. What it's about is the future of Florida."Graham described the ticket as centrist and moderate, with an agenda focused on housing affordability, education and healthcare access. She also promised to move Florida away from culture-war fights and what she called political interference in higher education.That appeal to voters outside the Democratic base will be essential. Florida had nearly 3.33 million voters registered with no party affiliation as of July 31, while Republicans held a registration advantage of more than 1.5 million over Democrats, according to the Florida Division of Elections.Democrats have not won a Florida governor's race since Lawton Chiles was reelected in 1994. The latest JMI survey showed Donalds leading Jolly 45 to 38 percent in a potential general-election matchup, with roughly one in six voters undecided.Florida's primary is Aug. The general election is Nov.

hero.headline: 16-year-old girl dies after falling through roof of abandoned Sebastian building
hero.teaser: A 16-year-old girl died after falling approximately 29 feet through a hole in the roof of an abandoned four-story building in Sebastian on Saturday night. Deputies said the group had been trespassing on the property.
hero.body:
A 16-year-old girl died after she fell through a hole in the roof of an abandoned four-story building last Saturday in Sebastian, deputies said. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office responded to 9846 Riverside Preserve Drive in Sebastian at about 10:35 p.m. after receiving a 911 call reporting that the girl had fallen from a concrete structure and was critically injured. Deputies arrived and found a group of minors along with the critically injured teen on the second floor of the abandoned building.

The investigation determined the group had been trespassing on the property and was on the roof when the teen fell through a hole in the roof, dropping approximately 29 feet to the floor below, the sheriff's office said. One of the minors in the group knew CPR and immediately began life-saving measures. The 16-year-old was flown to Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where she died from her injuries a short time later.

Detectives are actively investigating the teen's death, but said at this time, all evidence indicates this was an accident. The Indian River County Sheriff's Office extends its deepest sympathies to the family during this difficult time. We also want to remind the public, especially parents and teens, of the serious dangers posed by climbing on abandoned structures, and the legal consequences of trespassing on privately owned property, the sheriff's office said.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested in hit-and-run that seriously injured 7-year-old girl
cards.teaser: Demetrius Nathaniel Johnson, 34, was arrested on Aug. 5 following a hit-and-run accident that occurred on Aug. 1 in Fort Pierce where a 7-year-old girl was hospitalized. Surveillance video captured Johnson checking on the children before fleeing the scene.
cards.body:
Demetrius Nathaniel Johnson, 34, was arrested on Aug. 5 following a hit-and-run accident that occurred on Aug. 1 in Fort Pierce where a 7-year-old girl was hospitalized. Johnson was arrested at an apartment at the 2900 block of U.S. 1, Fort Pierce and charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury and driving while license suspended, a Fort Pierce Police news release stated.

The accident happened at about 8:55 p.m. at the intersection of North 25th Street and Avenue M, Fort Pierce, in which two children were crossing the road in a marked crosswalk when Johnson struck one of the children, according to police reports. Surveillance video obtained from a nearby business captured the crash and shows Johnson getting out of his car, described by witnesses as an early-2000s gold Mercedes-Benz, to check on the children before returning to his vehicle and fleeing the scene, according to police reports.

The suspect vehicle was identified using available investigative technology and law enforcement databases, which also assisted officers in identifying Johnson as the driver, police said in a press release. The seven-year-old victim has been released from the hospital and is currently recovering, according to police. Johnson is in the St. Lucie County Jail on no bond for those charges, according to the jail web site.

hero.headline: Indian River County schools avoid layoffs, give all teachers raises after budget reviews save $11 million
hero.body:
The School District of Indian River County will begin this school year with nearly fully staffed classrooms and no workforce reductions after annual budget reviews saved more than $11 million since 2019. Superintendent David Moore told CBS12 News that all teachers in the district are receiving raises, with teachers who have worked more than 10 years receiving roughly $2,200 and teachers with less classroom experience receiving approximately $1,300. Support staff will receive raises ranging from three to four percent.

Moore attributed the district's ability to avoid cuts to yearly budget reviews and reorganization that have helped maintain staffing and quality of education. The district currently has only five teacher vacancies. Moore said the district just finished negotiations with teachers and support staff unions and was able to provide additional compensation for their work.

The budget savings have also allowed the district to create more efficient school bus routes, reducing the number of buses on the road. Moore said he does not expect rising fuel prices to become an issue for the Indian River County School District.

The raises and staffing levels stand in contrast to many counties across Florida, where school districts have made workforce reductions this year. Moore said the annual review and reorganization of the budget have helped the district avoid cuts that could impact staffing and education quality.

He says the annual review and reorganization of the budget have helped the district avoid cuts that could impact staffing and, ultimately, the quality of education. We just finished negotiations with our teachers and support staff, unions, and were able to provide them additional compensation for the hard work that they do," Moore told CBS12 News. cards.headline: Indian River County schools plan to sell 10 properties including Rosewood Magnet School
cards.teaser: The School District of Indian River County is gauging interest from potential buyers for around 10 properties spread across the county, including four older schools, office buildings, and district-owned land.
cards.body:
The School District of Indian River County is looking to put around 10 properties on the market after consolidating multiple schools throughout the district. William Dodds, CFO of the School District of Indian River County, said the properties include four older schools, older office buildings, and district-owned land that are no longer necessary. Dodds said it is not the best financial decision to try to maintain two buildings where the district can operate in one.

Money made from the sale of the properties would go back to the district's capital budget to help keep buildings up, enhance some buildings, and fund capital projects the district would not be able to do otherwise. Ken Krasnow with Cushman and Wakefield, a real estate company working with the school district to sell the properties, said the buildings vary in condition and potential. Some buildings, like Rosewood Magnet School, could be transformed into medical office or quasi-flex space, while larger schools and properties could be redeveloped with commercial or retail along the front and residential in the back.

Dodds said the district is gauging interest from potential buyers before moving forward, and no decisions have been made yet. The district will reexamine interest in the properties and whether they need to be sold around December or January. The school board will have final approval.

hero.headline: 3 Port St. Lucie police officers placed on leave as FDLE investigates political campaign sign incidents
hero.body:
Three Port St. Lucie Police Department officers have been placed on paid administrative leave as investigations continue into two separate incidents involving political campaign signs that occurred last week on Southwest Airoso Boulevard. Lieutenant Aaron Martin, Lieutenant Jason Vega and Detective Sergeant Joseph Alves were placed on leave effective August 11, 2026.

Chief Leo Niemczyk made the decision following a review of the initial facts and timeline surrounding the incidents. Chief Niemczyk requested the Florida Department of Law Enforcement's assistance after determining it was the appropriate course of action, and FDLE agreed to take over the criminal investigation.

Following FDLE's completion of the criminal investigation, the Port St. Lucie Police Department will proceed with its internal investigation. The investigative process requires that the criminal investigation be completed before the internal administrative investigation begins.

The Port St. Lucie Police Department says it remains committed to ensuring all investigations are conducted fairly and impartially, maintaining its longstanding commitment to integrity, professionalism and accountability. The department will not provide additional information or comment on matters being handled by FDLE, and all questions regarding the criminal investigation should be directed to FDLE.

Chief Niemczyk requested the Florida Department of Law Enforcement's (FDLE) assistance after determining it was the appropriate course of action, and FDLE agreed to take over the criminal investigation. Following FDLE's completion of the criminal investigation, the Port St. Lucie Police Department will proceed with its internal investigation. The investigative process requires that the criminal investigation be completed before the internal administrative investigation begins. The Port St. Lucie Police Department says it remains committed to ensuring all investigations are conducted fairly and impartially, maintaining its longstanding commitment to integrity, professionalism and accountability.

cards.headline: Person shot and killed while attempting to enter residence at Seminole Mobile Home Park
cards.teaser: A person died after being shot while allegedly trying to enter a residence at the Seminole Mobile Home Park community in the 3300 block of Orange Avenue Wednesday night.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office responded to a shooting report at 9:11 p.m. Wednesday in the 3300 block of Orange Avenue at the Seminole Mobile Home Park community. Deputies and St. Lucie County Fire District personnel found one person suffering from a gunshot wound. The victim was taken to a local hospital where they later died from their injuries.

According to the initial 911 call, the person was shot while allegedly trying to enter a residence. Investigators obtained and executed a search warrant at the residence, recovering what they believe is the firearm used in the shooting. The scene was cleared shortly after 6 a.m. Thursday.

The sheriff's office said detectives are working to piece together the complete sequence of events that led to the shooting and determine why the person was at the residence. Investigators believe this was an isolated incident and say there is no immediate threat to the surrounding community. The sheriff's office is asking anyone with information about the shooting to call 772-462-3230 or submit anonymous tips through Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers at 800-273-TIPS.

hero.headline: Martin County deputies save senior citizen from $600,000 gold bar scam
hero.body:
A Martin County senior citizen nearly lost $600,000 to a gold bar scam before deputies intervened and helped stop the transaction. The victim was contacted by a fraudster claiming to be from his financial institution and was told that his bank account had been compromised, the Martin County Sheriff's Office said.

The scammer convinced the senior citizen that he needed to protect his money by backing it up with gold. The victim was instructed to send $600,000 to a legitimate gold vendor. The scammer told the victim that the gold would then be picked up by a third-party driver and delivered to the bank.

After going through with the transaction, the victim quickly realized something was not right and immediately went to his bank. The bank recognized the situation as potential fraud and advised him to contact the sheriff's office.

The responding deputy spoke directly with the gold vendor and helped the victim stop the transaction from going through. The victim confirmed he received a full refund of his $600,000, the Martin County Sheriff's Office said.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested in hit-and-run that seriously injured 7-year-old boy
hero.body:
The Fort Pierce Police Department arrested Demetrius Johnson in connection with an Aug. 1 hit-and-run crash that left a 7-year-old boy seriously injured. Johnson, 34, was arrested at 2905 U.S. Highway 1 and faces charges of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury and driving with a suspended license.

The crash occurred at 8:55 p.m. on Aug. 1 at the intersection of North 25th Street and Avenue M. Two children were crossing the roadway in a marked crosswalk when Johnson allegedly struck one of them. Surveillance video from a nearby business shows two children running across the street in the crosswalk as a vehicle makes a sharp left turn and strikes the 7-year-old boy.

Johnson is seen in the video briefly getting out of his vehicle to check on the child before returning to the vehicle and driving away. The 7-year-old boy has been released from the hospital and is recovering.

The investigation remains ongoing. The Fort Pierce Police Department has not released additional information about the case.

hero.headline: Indian River County deputies talk man off 17th Street Bridge after two-hour standoff
hero.body:
Indian River County deputies safely took a man into custody after a two-hour standoff on the 17th Street Bridge early Tuesday morning. The incident began around 1 a.m. when deputies responded to a call from Port St. Lucie police about a man wanted for burglary who had called his mother and told her he wanted to kill himself.

Body camera footage showed the man sitting on a platform over the bridge railing with his feet dangling in the air. Traffic Deputy Edouard Gast, a member of the Indian River County Sheriff's Office Crisis Negotiation Team, worked to establish a connection with the man. Gast said the man at first did not want to talk, and it took time to get him to open up. At one point, the man appeared ready to jump. Gast continued to plead with him, saying, "Come on, man, don't do this to your mom."

Gast said the man flipped a switch and climbed on top, positioning himself to jump. Gast talked to him repeatedly until the man climbed back over and stood on the platform. The sheriff's office marine unit and fire rescue crews were stationed in the water below as a safety precaution.

After two hours of negotiation, the man climbed back to the top of the bridge and shook the negotiator's hand. The man was taken into custody without incident. Sgt. from the sheriff's office said that even though the man was wanted out of Port St. Lucie, deputies still treated him with due care to make sure he was safe and could answer for his crimes.

cards.headline: Trail camera, AirTags fuel sign theft allegations between Martin County candidates
cards.teaser: A Martin County Commission candidate says he caught a campaign sign thief on a trail camera and tracked stolen signs with AirTags, igniting a public clash between political candidates in the final days before the August election.
cards.body:
Chris Collins, running for Martin County Commission Seat Two, posted a video to Facebook claiming he caught a man stealing his campaign signs using a hunting trail camera. In the video, Collins stands in front of a still photo showing a man in a darkened area at night holding one of his campaign signs. Collins, formerly the Mayor of Stuart, said he set up the trail cam after some of his signs went missing and put Apple AirTags on some of the signs to track their location.

Collins identified the man as Jim Gallegos and said the signs were tracked to Gallegos' house. Collins claimed Gallegos is a campaign advisor to Merritt Matheson, another political candidate, though not in the same race as Collins. Gallegos denied the accusation, saying he was taking down signs that the property owner had requested be removed. Merritt Matheson sent a text saying Gallegos is not his campaign advisor.

The story of the stolen signs prompted Derreck Ogden, who is running for election to be a Stuart City Commissioner, to confront Gallegos. Their argument about the campaign signs was caught on camera and posted on Facebook. Gallegos said he removed about 30 campaign signs for various candidates, not just Chris Collins' campaign, because the property owner did not want the signs on his property. Gallegos said he no longer has the campaign signs.

hero.headline: Palm City home condemned after woman charged with hoarding 36 Border Collies in 'worst case ever seen'
hero.body:
The Martin County Building Department condemned a Palm City home on Wednesday after authorities arrested Paige O'Donnell on 72 charges in connection with hoarding 36 Border Collies in what the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast called the worst animal hoarding case in its history. The notice posted to the gate states occupancy is prohibited as the structure is unfit for human occupancy under section 21.75.3, citing an unsanitary single-family residence.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office arrested O'Donnell on Monday following a lengthy investigation into animal welfare concerns at her residence. When deputies executed a search warrant, they discovered dogs covered in feces and urine living in a home with no functioning air conditioning and floors covered in waste and garbage, according to a probable cause affidavit. Deputies noted the condition of the dogs and surrounding environment was such that the animals were difficult to distinguish from the heavily soiled areas of the residence.

Animal Control Officer Tabitha Queen documented approximately 20 related incidents at the address spanning from 2020 through 2026. During an August 3 meeting at Jock Leighton Park in Palm City, O'Donnell told the officer she owned only four dogs, but records from Boulevard Animal Hospital identified approximately 38 adult dogs associated with O'Donnell. The clinic employee said there were so many puppies brought in with O'Donnell that it was impossible to get an accurate count, with the last recorded visit on June 25, 2022.

O'Donnell faces 72 total charges, including 36 counts of felony animal cruelty and 36 misdemeanor counts for failing to provide the dogs with proper exercise or air. A judge set her total bond at $275,000 and ordered that she may not own or possess any animals as a condition of her bond. The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is providing urgent care for the 36 Border Collies, including three puppies up to six months old, with staff working around the clock to medically groom, bathe and examine the dogs.

hero.headline: Indian River County school district plans to sell around 10 properties including 4 older schools
hero.teaser: The School District of Indian River County is looking to put around 10 properties on the market for potential buyers, including 4 older schools, older office buildings and district-owned land.
hero.body:
William Dodds, CFO of the School District of Indian River County, said the properties are spread across the county and include 4 older schools, older office buildings and district-owned land. After consolidating multiple schools throughout the district, Dodds said some of the properties are no longer necessary. Money made from the sale of the properties would go back to the district's capital budget to help keep buildings up, enhance some buildings and do things in capital that the district would not be able to do otherwise.

Ken Krasnow with Cushman and Wakefield, a real estate company working with the school district to sell the properties, said the buildings vary in condition and potential. Krasnow said some buildings, like Rosewood Magnet School, could be transformed into medical office or quasi-flex space. Krasnow said larger schools and properties could be redeveloped with commercial and retail along the front and residential in the back.

No decisions have been made yet. Dodds said the district is gauging interest from potential buyers before moving forward. Dodds said the district will reexamine interest in the properties and whether they need to be sold around December or January. The school board will have final approval.

cards.headline: Indian River County Sheriff's Office locates truck in deadly Vero Beach e-bike hit-and-run
cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office has located the vehicle allegedly involved in a deadly hit-and-run crash that killed a 48-year-old Vero Beach man riding an electric bicycle Sunday night near 8th Street and 14th Avenue. An IRCSO analyst located a vehicle matching the truck's description, including a missing passenger-side mirror, while reviewing leads with the Florida Highway Patrol. Deputies used Flock Safety technology and other investigative resources to identify the vehicle, its license plate and information about the driver.

The crash occurred at about 8:57 p.m. Sunday when the man was riding an e-bike near 8th Street and 14th Avenue. Investigators said a light-colored Ford F-150, believed to be a 2015 to 2020 model, was traveling behind the man in the same lane. As the pickup approached the bicyclist, the driver took evasive action, traveling southwest and partially entering the eastbound lane. However, the driver was unable to avoid the bicyclist, and the right side of the pickup struck him.

The bicyclist was thrown onto the roadway and came to rest in the eastbound lane of 8th Street. FHP said the driver fled the scene without rendering aid or contacting law enforcement. The bicyclist was taken to Lawnwood Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

The information from IRCSO's Real Time Crime Center allowed FHP to locate the vehicle and confirm its connection to the crash. IRCSO has not identified the driver or released the identity of the bicyclist who was killed.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce police arrest man in hit-and-run that seriously injured 7-year-old boy
hero.body:
The Fort Pierce Police Department arrested a man in connection with an Aug. 1 hit-and-run crash that left a 7-year-old boy seriously injured. Police arrested Demetrius Johnson at 2905 U.S. Highway 1 and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury and driving with a suspended license.

The crash occurred at 8:55 p.m. on Aug. 1 at the intersection of North 25th Street and Avenue M in Fort Pierce. Two children were crossing the roadway in a marked crosswalk when Johnson struck one of them, according to police.

Surveillance video from a nearby business shows two children running across the street in the crosswalk as a vehicle makes a sharp left turn and strikes the 7-year-old boy. Johnson, 34, briefly exited his vehicle to check on the child before returning to the vehicle and driving away, police said.

The 7-year-old boy has been released from the hospital and is recovering. The investigation remains ongoing, and anyone with additional information is asked to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department at 772-462-6800 or Treasure Coast Crime Stoppers.

hero.headline: South Fork High School freshman describes hot, crowded bus ride on first day of school
hero.teaser: A Martin County parent says her daughter came home in tears after her first bus ride home from South Fork High School, describing extreme heat and overcrowding on the bus Monday.
hero.body:
Sherri Lindemann's daughter is a freshman at South Fork High School. Lindemann said she was caught off guard when she learned what had upset her child. Lindemann said her daughter described a miserable experience on the ride. She said the bus was extremely hot with no air or ventilation and that there was overcrowding with four kids to every seat, with everybody sweaty and upset. The bus ride took an hour and 15 minutes to get home.

The Martin County School District said it understands why the experience would be concerning for students and families, especially on the first day of school when routines are new and students are adjusting to the year ahead. The district's Transportation team confirmed that 57 students were on the bus on Monday, which falls within regulation for high school buses, and that no seat had 4 students in it. Staff also confirmed the bus's air conditioning system was operating properly, but the district acknowledged that mid-August heat can make any bus ride feel particularly warm.

Lindemann's concerns come after the school district consolidated 3 school bus routes to make transportation more efficient without impacting students. In a statement, the district said the delays had nothing to do with the consolidation. The district said Transportation staff are closely monitoring ridership and routes as drivers become more familiar with traffic patterns and students become accustomed to safely exiting the bus. Families can track their child's bus through the MyReaxiumApp. Those who need help setting up an account can contact the transportation department at 772-219-1287.

hero.headline: Republicans Build 40,000-Vote Lead in Florida Primary as Democrats Turn Out at Higher Rate
hero.body:
Republicans hold a 40,114-vote lead over Democrats in Florida's primary election with less than a week before Election Day, even as Democrats vote at a significantly higher rate relative to their party registration, according to Fresh Take Florida's statewide turnout tracker.

As of 3:30 p.m. Wednesday, more than 1.3 million Floridians had already voted. Republicans accounted for 585,423 ballots compared with 545,309 Democrats. Another 177,542 ballots came from voters outside the two major parties. Republicans enter this election with a registration advantage of roughly 1.54 million voters, with 5.6 million registered Republicans and 4.06 million Democrats. Democrats still lead in mail ballots, with 409,358 Democrats voting by mail compared with 356,500 Republicans, a Democratic lead of 52,858 ballots. Republicans have overwhelmed that advantage at early voting sites, where 228,923 Republicans have voted early in person compared with 135,951 Democrats, a GOP advantage of 92,972 votes.

When turnout is measured against the size of each party, 13.43 percent of registered Democrats have voted compared with 10.45 percent of registered Republicans, almost a three-percentage-point Democratic advantage. About 10.08 percent of registered Democrats have already voted by mail compared with 6.37 percent of Republicans. Republicans have the edge in early in-person participation, 4.09 percent to 3.35 percent. Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried said the political environment is shifting and argued the Republican supermajority in the Legislature is breakable this cycle. Republican Party of Florida Chair Evan Power said Republicans have taken the vote lead and will not look back, predicting a big vote lead on Election Day.

Florida's primary Election Day is August 18, with the state's mandatory early voting period continuing through Saturday, August 15. Political analyst Susan MacManus said enthusiasm only matters if campaigns can turn it into votes. For Democrats, the challenge is proving that dissatisfaction over affordability and the party in power can translate into enough turnout to overcome Florida's Republican registration advantage. For Republicans, it is showing that their larger voter pool and established turnout operation can dominate when all ballots are counted.

cards.headline: Florida Homeowners with Aging Roofs Face Rising Insurance Premiums as Companies Limit Coverage
cards.teaser: Insurance companies increasingly raise premiums on asphalt shingle roofs older than 15 years, while metal roofs receive favorable treatment for their 30-year-plus lifespan.
cards.body:
Florida homeowners insurance premiums largely depend on two critical roof factors: age and materials, according to local insurance experts who say the roof serves as a home's primary defense against weather damage. Insurance companies increasingly raise premiums on asphalt shingle roofs older than 15 years, while metal roofs receive favorable treatment for their 30-year-plus lifespan, according to industry professionals. Homeowners with shingle roofs over 15 years face shrinking insurance options, explained Lee Wiglesworth of Wiglesworth-Rindom Insurance in Stuart.

Asphalt shingles remain Florida's most popular and economical roofing choice, but their vulnerability to heat and wind makes them less attractive to insurers as they age. Companies with the most competitive rates only want roofs under 15 years old, so homeowners with 16-year-old roofs can still have options but are starting to eliminate options for themselves, Wiglesworth said. For homeowners reluctant to replace aging roofs, scheduled endorsements offer partial protection. Under this arrangement, insurers cover only 25 percent of an older roof's value while homeowners self-insure the remaining 75 percent.

Metal roofs cost nearly twice as much as asphalt shingles but offer superior long-term protection and insurance advantages, according to Wiglesworth. Florida's insurance market has seen new companies enter the state, with more insurers willing to cover older homes. His advice for homeowners considering roof replacement: call an agent who can shop multiple carriers and ask what it would save them if they got a new roof, even before they get a new roof.

hero.headline: Indian River County school district plans to sell 10 properties across county
hero.body:
The School District of Indian River County is looking to put around 10 properties on the market for potential buyers. The properties are spread across the county and include four older schools, older office buildings, and district-owned land, according to William Dodds, CFO of the School District of Indian River County.

Dodds said the properties are no longer necessary after the district consolidated multiple schools. The district is gauging interest from potential buyers before moving forward, and no decisions have been made yet. Money made from the sale of the properties would go back to the district's capital budget.

Ken Krasnow with Cushman and Wakefield, a real estate company working with the school district to sell the properties, said the buildings vary in condition and potential. Some buildings, like Rosewood Magnet School, could be transformed into medical office or flex space. Larger schools and properties could be redeveloped with commercial or retail space along the front and residential in the back.

Dodds said the district will reexamine interest in the properties and whether they need to be sold around December or January. The school board will have final approval. The capital budget funds would help keep district buildings up and enhance facilities.

hero.headline: Truck located in deadly Vero Beach e-bike hit-and-run that killed 48-year-old man
hero.teaser: The Indian River County Sheriff's Office has located the vehicle allegedly involved in a deadly hit-and-run crash that killed a man riding an electric bicycle Sunday night in Vero Beach.
hero.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff's Office located the vehicle allegedly involved in a deadly hit-and-run crash that killed a 48-year-old Vero Beach man riding an electric bicycle Sunday night. The sheriff's office Real Time Crime Center worked with the Florida Highway Patrol since the crash to locate the vehicle involved, and an analyst located a vehicle matching the truck's description, including a missing passenger-side mirror.

Deputies used Flock Safety technology and other investigative resources to identify the vehicle, its license plate and information about the driver. The information allowed FHP to locate the vehicle and confirm its connection to the crash. At about 8:57 p.m. Sunday, the man was riding an e-bike near 8th Street and 14th Avenue when he was struck by what investigators believed was a light-colored Ford F-150, believed to be a 2015 to 2020 model, traveling behind him in the same lane.

As the pickup approached the bicyclist, the driver took evasive action, traveling southwest and partially entering the eastbound lane. Troopers said the driver was unable to avoid the bicyclist, and the right side of the pickup struck him. The bicyclist was thrown onto the roadway and came to rest in the eastbound lane of 8th Street. FHP said the driver fled the scene without rendering aid or contacting law enforcement. The bicyclist was taken to Lawnwood Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

cards.headline: 36 dogs rescued from Palm City home face long recovery at Humane Society of Treasure Coast
cards.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is working around the clock to medically groom, bathe and examine 36 Border Collies rescued from a Palm City home, with many suffering from eye and skin infections.
cards.body:
A Palm City woman is in custody on a $270,000 bond after authorities discovered 36 Border Collies living in severe neglect inside her home on Alligator Street, leading to 72 charges of animal cruelty. Martin County Sheriff John Budensiek said the animals were in deplorable conditions. All 36 dogs are now being cared for at the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast.

Sarah Fisher, a spokesperson for the organization, described the severity of the animals' condition. The shelter found not only matted and underweight dogs with skin issues, but also glass and metal embedded in their fur. The dogs' tongues were bleeding from them biting their tongues, there was feces in their mouths, and their tails might be falling off, Fisher said. The shaving process can take an hour per dog, and as staff members cut and shave, they are finding lots of pieces of rusted metal, sharp metal, and shards of glass stuck in the dogs' fur.

Fisher said some of the dogs are just laying there and don't know what to do. They don't know to lift their head and don't know how to interact with people, showing they were institutionalized. The case dates back to 2020, when animal services first investigated Paige O'Donnell's home and dogs. Court records show complaints continued through 2022 and 2023, with renewed concerns in 2026 leading to surveillance and multiple attempted inspections. The Humane Society said it could take time before the dogs are ready for foster homes or adoption and is asking for community support to help with the recovery efforts.

Court records show complaints continued through 2022 and 2023, with renewed concerns in 2026 leading to surveillance and multiple attempted inspections. After officers observed one dog this month, they obtained a search warrant, which led to the discovery of the 36 dogs and O'Donnell’s arrest. During her first court appearance, O'Donnell was ordered, "You may not possess either temporarily or permanently any animals as a condition of your bond." We had their tongues were bleeding from them biting their tongues. There was feces in their mouths. Their tails might be falling off. I mean, it's the worst that I've seen," Fisher said. Fisher added that the focus is currently on assessing each dog’s physical and mental health. "Some of the dogs are just laying there, and they don't know what to do. They don't know to lift their head. They don't know how to interact with people. So you can tell they were institutionalized," Fisher said. Reflecting on the situation, Fisher said, "I don't know whether to be sad for her or angry. Because, you know, at one time in her life, she loved these dogs and she put everything towards these dogs.
