hero.headline: Fort Pierce approves 36-unit temporary family housing at GraceWay Village on Hartman Road
hero.body:
The Fort Pierce City Commission voted unanimously on August 3 to approve a major site plan and conditional use permit allowing GraceWay Village, Inc. to construct 36 dwelling units of temporary family housing at 1780 Hartman Road. The project will be built on 7.84 acres near the nonprofit's existing cafe and clothing boutique, with a density of 4.5 units per acre, well below the maximum of 15 units per acre allowed under the city's comprehensive plan for general commercial land use.

The development will proceed in three phases. Phase 1 will occupy 10,200 square feet and contain 10 dwelling units with support facilities. Phase 2 will add six buildings totaling 17,800 square feet, with each building containing three dwelling units. Phase 3 will expand the first facility by 6,300 square feet, adding eight additional dwelling units and support facilities. Each unit will be approximately 990 square feet, and 73.72 percent of the site will remain open space.

Assistant Planning Director Chris Suneson told the commission that the project met all code requirements and had been coordinated with the Technical Review Committee, with all departments supporting the application. St. Lucie County has required the applicant to provide a sidewalk in front of the property from north to south. The Planning Board had previously recommended approval unanimously at a July 13 meeting.

GraceWay Village CEO Chrystal Netherton told the Planning Board in July that the facility focuses on temporary stays to help families become self-sufficient. Project Engineer Mark Landsman said many residents might only need a three-month stay. Commissioner Chris Dzadovsky made the motion for approval on August 3, which was seconded by Commissioner Michael Broderick and passed unanimously.
hero.article_text: The current view of the 7.84-acre property at 1780 Hartman Road owned by the not for profit Graceway Village. The City Commission voted unanimously Aug.3 to recommend to approve a major site plan and conditional use permit to enable GraceWay Village, Inc. to construct 36 dwelling units of temporary family housing on Hartman Road. The location of the 7.84 acre property at 1780 Hartman Road owned by the not-for-profit Graceway Village. The Fort Pierce City Commission voted unanimously Aug. 3 to approve a major site plan and conditional use permit to enable GraceWay Village, Inc. to construct 36 dwelling units of temporary family housing on the parcel. FORT PIERCE – The City Commission voted unanimously Aug. 3 to approve a major site plan and conditional use permit to enable GraceWay Village, Inc. to construct temporary congregate housing for adults and families on Hartman Road near the non-profit entity’s existing cafe and clothing boutique. The Planning Board previously heard the same requests on July 13, unanimously recommending approval. Assistant Planning Director Chris Suneson introduced the agenda item during the latest meeting. “This is a request this evening to review and approve an application for a major site plan with conditional use to allow adult congregate living facilities at 1780 Hartman Road,” he said. “The owner of Graceway Village Inc. proposes to construct a family shelter community centered on temporary housing with associated site improvements on 7.84 acres. The property contains two buildings [with] a combined 7,563 square feet that houses the applicant’s cafe program, clothing boutique and offices. The facilities were remodeled in 2009 and got some roofing permits in 2021.” Suneson proceeded to emphasize that the property’s underlying General Commercial Future Land Use enabled the location of just such a congregate living facility on the parcel as a conditional use. “The land development code sets forth several basic standards that adult congregant living facilities must meet,” he continued. “The most important of these is that maximum residential densities may not exceed the level determined by the comprehensive plan for general commercial. That maximum is 15 dwelling units to the acre, and with the proposed 36 dwelling units, the project has a density of 4.5 units to the acre.” The assistant planning director also described the site plan, which the applicant proposes to construct in three separate phases. “Phase 1 occupies 10,200 square feet and contains 10 dwelling units and support facilities,” he explained. “Phase 2 contemplates six additional buildings, comprising 17,800 square feet, with each building containing three dwelling units. The final phase is an expansion of the first facility with tri-plex cottages. Each unit will be about 990 square feet. It is an extension of the Phase 1 building, which would expand the family shelter building by an additional 6,300 square feet while also providing eight additional dwelling units and support facilities. Most of the site, 73.72 percent, will be left to open space. This project has been coordinated with the Technical Review Committee [and] all departments have supported the application.” Commissioner Michael Broderick was the first Board member to comment afterward and pose a question to Suneson. “If it was our job to just sit up here and rate the application based on need in the community, this would receive 110 percent approval,” he said. “However, that’s not what we’re here to do: We’re here to participate in a quasi-judicial hearing and determine facts. I reviewed this application in detail, site plans, everything. My only question is, is there any portion of the code that you’re aware of that this application does not meet?” “Not that I’m aware of sir,” Suneson replied. Commissioner Chris Dzadovsky raised a question to staff. “Due to the future use of this, congregant living and the possibility of families, is there any provision for transportation at this location, a local bus set aside for transportation?” he asked. Suneson did not have a positive reply to him on that inquiry, however, instead describing other planned improvements on the parcel. “First off, I do not believe this is on a public bus route,” he said. “Second, the applicant has been required by St. Lucie County to provide a sidewalk in front of the property from north to south. Thirdly, if you’re talking about private facilities, I think there’s plentiful parking and driveway access in order to provide that type of service if it’s contemplated in the future by the applicant.” GraceWay Village’s contracted Landscape Architect Brad Currie also addressed the Commission. “Tonight, I’m very grateful to be representing GraceWay Village and their request to expand their existing facility,” he said. Broderick, this is one of the few projects that I’ve brought before the City Commission that I didn’t think you were going to have any comments on, and you did still.” The commissioner, however, admitted this particular development had no apparent controversy or protest. “We usually tend to have a little bit of a friction point, but on this, I think we’re all in agreement,” Broderick explained. “I actually think this is a great location for the project.” Currie did acknowledge some concerns expressed by Planning Board member Krista Story on July 13 about potentially locating so much residential in a commercial use. The applicant’s contracted Project Engineer Mark Landsman attempted to allay her fears that same night. “This is not a permanent residence,” he said during the prior meeting. “These are temporary residences to help people get back on their feet, so it’s not going to be a long-term resident.” While GraceWay Village CEO Chrystal Netherton did not come to the podium during the Commission meeting, she did addressed Storey’s concerns as well during the Planning Board meeting. “The first day of coming to Graceway Village, we are talking about your exit strategy to get into your own permanent housing,” she said July 13. “This really is an opportunity for this family to be self-sufficient [and] learn the skills. Many of them might only need a three-month stay with us.” After no member of the public came forward to comment on Aug. 3, Commissioner Dzadovsky made a motion for approval, with was seconded by Commissioner Broderick and passed unanimously. hero.headline: Indian River County schools launch real-time bus tracking feature for parents
hero.teaser: The School District of Indian River County is rolling out a new feature in its free app this school year that allows parents to track their child's bus in real time and receive push notifications when buses are running late.
hero.body:
The School District of Indian River County is rolling out a new feature in its free app this school year that allows parents to track their child's bus in real time. Parents can tap the bus icon in the district's app to see where the bus is and get an estimated arrival time. The app will also send push notifications when a bus is running late.

Superintendent David K. Moore says the new feature is designed to give parents more peace of mind. "You feel good as a parent, speaking as a parent, when your kid's in school. But when they are on the bus, there's just a little bit of angst until they get off that bus and walk in that front door," Moore told CBS12 News. "Now parents have greater access when they are walking in that front door."

The district is also adding another layer of security for students. Students will scan their school ID when they board the bus, allowing the district to keep better track of who is riding each bus. Moore says every school bus driver position is filled, meaning the district is fully staffed.

cards.headline: Troopers seek Ford F-150 driver after deadly e-bike hit-and-run in Vero Beach
cards.body:
A 48-year-old Vero Beach man riding an electric bicycle was killed after being struck by a pickup truck that fled the scene Sunday night in unincorporated Indian River County. The Florida Highway Patrol said the crash happened around 8:57 p.m. Sunday at the intersection of 8th Street and 14th Avenue.

The man was traveling west on an e-bike in the westbound lane of 8th Street as he approached 14th Avenue. A light-colored Ford F-150, believed to be a 2015 to 2020 model, was traveling behind him in the same lane. As the truck approached the bicyclist, the driver took evasive action and moved southwest, partially entering the eastbound lane. The truck still struck the bicyclist with its right side. The man was thrown onto the roadway and came to rest in the eastbound lane.

The driver fled without stopping to provide aid or contact law enforcement. Investigators say the truck may be missing its right-side rearview mirror due to the crash. The bicyclist was taken to Lawnwood Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

hero.headline: Centennial High School student hit by car at Port St. Lucie intersection
hero.body:
A 16-year-old Centennial High School student was hit by a vehicle Monday morning while crossing against the pedestrian signal at the intersection of Crosstown Parkway and SW Cameo Boulevard in Port St. Lucie. The crash occurred shortly after 7 a.m., according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

The preliminary investigation indicates the teenager attempted to cross Crosstown Parkway against the pedestrian signal, entering the roadway in front of oncoming traffic that had the right of way. The teen told investigators they believed they could make it across the street before an approaching vehicle reached them. The driver was unable to avoid striking the student.

The 16-year-old sustained superficial injuries but declined medical transport at the scene. The teen's guardians were notified of the incident. The vehicle involved in the crash sustained minor cosmetic damage.

In March 2024, a 15-year-old student was hit by a car making a right turn onto Crosstown Parkway at Southwest Cameo Boulevard and was taken to the hospital with minor injuries.

cards.teaser: A new boutique offering Fort Pierce souvenirs, locally made gifts, and Florida-inspired apparel opened on Second Street in early June.
cards.body:
Sunshine State of Mind Boutique opened in early June on Second Street in downtown Fort Pierce, offering Fort Pierce souvenirs, locally made works of art, and Florida-inspired apparel and gifts. The shop is owned by Kim Brant, who has worked in downtown Fort Pierce for many years, including 10 years at the Original Tiki Bar and the past five years at Cobbs Landing.

Brant said she saw the need for a shop dedicated to showcasing the city's charm and character. She designs most of the shirts and sweatshirts herself and keeps vendors as local as possible. One wall features a shelf labeled Locals Only, showcasing work by local artists and crafters.

Sunshine State of Mind Boutique is located at 102 N. 2nd St., Unit B, Fort Pierce. The shop is a family affair, with Brant's husband Chris and their children helping so she can continue working at Cobbs Landing.

hero.headline: Martin County schools cut three bus routes, saving $255,000 annually as students return
hero.body:
Martin County Public Schools reduced its bus routes from 58 to 55 as students returned to classrooms Monday, a move the school board voted to approve that will save the district $255,000 per year. Superintendent Michael Maine said the district is combining underused routes serving the same areas rather than eliminating any stops, and every bus will continue to operate within its legal capacity.

Maine said the district is right-sizing its transportation system because it does not make sense to have 16 or 20 students on a 77-passenger bus. Some routes may take a little longer, but drivers will be paid for any additional time they work. All buses have seatbelts, and depending on the age, students have to be buckled up.

The district will never run a transportation route or a bus that is over capacity, Maine said. While bus stops are not changing, some students may see a different bus number this year. The transportation department reports all 55 bus routes are covered with 56 drivers available.

Maine said families should expect the usual first-week delays as drivers settle into their new routes. Parents can check their child's bus assignment in the focus parent portal or track their bus in real time using the MyReaxium app. Some employees have raised concerns about what the route cuts could mean for already-crowded buses.

cards.article_text: Martin County Public Schools has earned its second consecutive A rating from the state, marking a significant turnaround from seven years of B-level performance through innovative teaching methods that prioritize individual student needs over traditional classroom instruction. Superintendent Michael Maine announced the district's back-to-back A grades for the 2024-25 and 2025-26 school years, crediting teachers and administrators who shifted away from whole-group instruction to personalized learning approaches that close achievement gaps The transformation centers on what Maine calls a "game changer" — moving beyond traditional classroom lectures to small-group instruction tailored to each student's skill level. "Instead of focusing on all whole group instruction, when the teacher is standing up in front of the classroom and just teaching the entire class, that's happening to introduce lessons," Maine explained. "But teachers are spending a lot more time individualizing the instruction for individual kids, pulling small groups, having smaller groups of students around the kidney table with them." Teachers now use education technology to track student progress in real-time and intervene quickly when students struggle. The data-driven approach allows educators to identify learning gaps and provide targeted remediation through small-group sessions. Martin County's success comes as Florida school districts face increasing pressure to improve academic outcomes while managing budget constraints and staffing challenges. The district's model demonstrates how strategic teaching methods can drive measurable results without reducing class sizes or significantly increasing costs. The district maintains regular class sizes mandated by state rules but transforms instruction delivery through centers and rotations that keep all students engaged at appropriate levels. "The teachers are doing a really good job making sure that while he or she's pulling a small group of students, the other students are also in groups working on things that they need," Maine said. Students rotate through differentiated instruction centers, with some working on advanced materials while others receive targeted support. Martin County enters the new school year nearly fully staffed, with 29 teaching vacancies remaining as of early August, with 16 candidates already in the onboarding process. Maine expects the district to be "in a really, really good position" when students return August 10. The transportation department reports all 55 bus routes covered with 56 drivers available. Student enrollment remains steady at approximately 16,000 students, consistent with recent years. Construction continues at Murray Middle School following significant tornado damage that destroyed two buildings and severely damaged a third. The multi-phase rebuilding project will deliver new facilities including band and chorus rooms, agricultural education spaces, a media center, administrative building, and additional classroom space. Maine said certain construction phases will be completed by December 2027, with others finishing by August 2027, depending on progress. The district launched a flexible education program, dubbed "flex tech," offering families alternatives including single-course enrollment, partial schedules, and fully virtual learning through Martin eSchool. "We really truly want to be the premier choice, the first choice for all of our families here in Martin County," Maine said. The program targets homeschool families who may need specific courses like advanced chemistry or algebra while maintaining connection to the district. Traditional high school students can also access evening courses or additional classes to enhance their academic preparation. Martin County continues expanding career and technical education programs that provide pathways to skilled trades and high-paying positions immediately after graduation. Programs include HVAC technician training, certified welding, construction trades, certified nursing assistant certification, drone flight operations, and entrepreneurship courses. "We have a lot of students that might want to go into a skilled trade right after high school and earn a really high-paying earning job," Maine said. The district continuously evaluates and upgrades security systems, including additional cameras, updated crisis alert badges, hardened front offices, and perimeter fencing improvements. "We're always going to be thinking first and foremost about the safety of our students," Maine said. "Anytime we see an area that needs to be improved, our safety and security team is quick to move in and get those fixed." Maine emphasized the district's commitment to living within its means while protecting classroom instruction from budget reductions. "We are great stewards of their taxpayer dollars. We do not spend more than we bring in," he said. Any operational adjustments have occurred at the district office level or through efficiency measures, not classroom programs. Looking ahead, Maine set an ambitious target for Martin County to rank among Florida's top 10 school districts while maintaining its A rating. "I want to be in the top 10 school districts in the state of Florida. We're working our way towards that goal," he said, emphasizing continuous improvement and professional development for staff. hero.headline: Man rescues woman trapped on railroad crossing in Hobe Sound
hero.body:
Josiah Baur rescued a woman whose car became stuck on train tracks at Bridge Road and Dixie Highway in Hobe Sound on Friday evening. Debbie Spoelstra was turning onto Bridge Road from Dixie Highway when a railroad crossing arm came down on her car, trapping her between the gates as a freight train approached. Baur was on his way home to Port St. Lucie when he stopped at the crossing and saw Spoelstra's red car stuck on the tracks.

Baur put his car in park and ran across the tracks to help. He lifted the crossing gate with both arms, allowing Spoelstra to back her car away from the tracks seconds before the train passed through. Dash camera video captured the rescue. Lizzy Dominguez, who witnessed the incident from behind Baur's car, posted a photo of Baur on social media to find and thank him.

Spoelstra said the crossing arm got stuck on her car antenna when she tried to reverse, preventing her from moving. She said she was not texting or distracted while driving and was taken off guard by the railroad crossing arms lowering. Witnesses reported the crossing arm malfunctioned during the incident. Spoelstra reported the malfunction to Florida East Coast Railway, which told her someone would inspect the gate.

Spoelstra and Baur met again at the railroad crossing on Sunday and hugged when they saw each other. Spoelstra said her baby grandson shares the same name as Baur. Both attributed the rescue to faith and said they have bonded over the experience. Spoelstra urged other drivers to always be careful and look both ways before crossing train tracks.
hero.article_text: An act of bravery and compassion is bringing two strangers together on the Treasure Coast. A young man rescued a woman whose car got stuck on a railroad crossing in Hobe Sound, saving her from near disaster. Stay up-to-date: The latest headlines and weather from WPBF 25 Just a few days ago, Josiah Baur and Debbie Spoelstra didn’t know each other, but now, they share a special connection. “Friday, I was leaving work, and I was heading back home. I was trying to get home for a tire appointment, funny enough, and running late for it. Train crossing went down, and I looked down on my phone, and I glimpsed up, and I saw the car stuck behind the railroad crossing,” Baur said. Spoelstra was still inside that car, stuck on the train tracks at Bridge Road and Dixie Highway in Hobe Sound. What I did is, I put my car in reverse, and apparently the gate got stuck on top of my car on the antenna. So, when I tried to reverse, it would not let me reverse. I sat there, I saw the train,” Spoelstra said. Baur, realizing she was still in the car, didn’t hesitate and jumped out of his car to help. “I threw it in park and just took off running. Try to see what side the train was on to see if it would clear her or not. But it was on her side and didn't really want to take a chance. So, I ran across and tried to push up on the thingy to release her,” Baur said. That split-second decision helped to avoid what could have been a devastating crash from a freight train. “He came just like a hero. And lifted the gate up off of my car. And I was able to reverse and get off the tracks. And as soon as he did that, within seconds, the train passed by me. So it was very scary, you know, life-changing experience for me,” Spoelstra said. “We think of heroes, I think police officers and military, not what I did. It was just a good, good thing to do,” Baur said. The two said they’ve now bonded over this unique experience, attributing it to their shared faith. “He was put in one place, I was put in one place, and it was just fate. And it was a God thing, you know, and then once I told him my grandson was Josiah, and then he was just like, ‘Oh, wow. It's definitely a God thing.’ So, I don't know. I would just say, like I said, I'm so grateful for him,” Spoelstra said. He puts us exactly where we need to be. If you're running late for something, it's probably for a reason. Just trust his plan,” Baur said. Spoelstra said she wasn’t texting or distracted while driving and was simply just taken off guard by the railroad crossing arms lowering. She wants to pass this message on to other drivers: always be careful and look both ways before crossing train tracks. Get the latest news updates with the WPBF 25 News app.

hero.headline: Man rescues woman trapped on railroad tracks in Hobe Sound
hero.body:
Josiah Baur rescued a woman whose car became trapped on railroad tracks at Bridge Road and Dixie Highway in Hobe Sound on Friday evening. Debbie Spoelstra was turning from Dixie Highway onto Bridge Road when a railroad crossing arm came down on her car, trapping her vehicle between the gates as a train approached. Baur, 23, was driving home to Port St. Lucie from work when he stopped at the crossing and saw Spoelstra stuck on the tracks on the opposite side.

Baur ran across the tracks and lifted the crossing gate with both arms, allowing Spoelstra to back her car off the tracks seconds before the train passed. Dash-cam video captured the moments as the train horn sounded and the locomotive moved closer to Spoelstra's red car while Baur ran toward the crossing. Another witness, Lizzy Dominguez, was stopped behind Baur's car and photographed him after the rescue, posting the image on social media to find and thank him.

Spoelstra and Baur met again at the railroad crossing on Sunday and embraced. Spoelstra said she was not texting or distracted while driving and was taken off guard by the crossing arms lowering. She reported the malfunctioning crossing arm to Florida East Coast Railway, which told her someone would inspect the gate.

Baur said he first checked which side of the tracks the train was approaching from before deciding to act. Spoelstra's grandson shares the name Josiah, a connection both she and Baur attributed to faith. Spoelstra urged other drivers to always be careful and look both ways before crossing train tracks.

hero.headline: Man lifts railroad crossing gate to rescue woman trapped on tracks in Hobe Sound
hero.body:
A 23-year-old man lifted a railroad crossing gate with his bare hands Friday evening to free a woman whose car became trapped on the tracks as a train approached on Bridge Road in Hobe Sound. Josiah Baur was driving home to Port St. Lucie from work when he stopped at the railroad crossing and saw Debbie Spoelstra's red car stuck between the crossing gates. A railroad crossing arm had come down on her car as she turned onto Bridge Road from Dixie Highway, and dash-cam video captured a train horn blaring as the train moved closer.

Baur ran across the tracks toward the crossing. He lifted the gate with both arms, giving Spoelstra enough time to back her car away from the tracks before the train came through. Spoelstra said she was frozen in her car until she saw Baur running toward her. Another witness, Lizzy Dominguez, was behind Baur's car and posted his photo on social media to find and thank him.

Spoelstra and Baur met again at the railroad crossing Sunday and hugged. Spoelstra called Baur a true American hero and said she believes things could have turned out very differently if he had not been there. Baur said he was fortunate that God put him where he was at that moment.

Witnesses said the crossing arm malfunctioned during the incident. Spoelstra reported the problem to Florida East Coast Railway and was told someone would come out to inspect the gate. Spoelstra said her baby grandson shares the same name as the man who rescued her.
hero.article_text: What started as a routine drive home from work turned into a terrifying race against time for Debbie Spoelstra. Spoelstra says she was turning onto Bridge Road from Dixie Highway in Hobe Sound Friday evening when a railroad crossing arm suddenly came down on her car, leaving her trapped on the tracks. Dash-cam video captured the tense moments that followed. A train's horn can be heard as it quickly moved closer and closer to Spoelstra's red car as it sat between the crossing gates. Then, a young man runs toward her. I was pretty much frozen, Spoelstra said. Then I thought about getting out of the car, and then at that moment I saw Josiah running across the railroad tracks. That man was 23-year-old Josiah Baur. Baur said he left work late that evening and was on his way home to Port Saint Lucie when he stopped at the crossing. He was on the other side of the tracks when he saw what was happening. You only get a couple seconds to react, Baur said. He immediately ran toward the crossing. I just took off running, he said. Baur reached the crossing and lifted the gate with both arms, giving Spoelstra enough time to back her car away from the tracks before the train came through. He said he first looked to see where the train was. It was on her side, so I ran up and pushed up on it and released it just in time for her to back up, Baur said. Another witness, Lizzy Dominguez, was behind Baur's car when she saw what was happening. She and the others in her car could only watch. We were just saying, Please, God, please, God, please, God,’ Dominguez said. We were frozen in the car. After the rescue, Dominguez took a photo of Baur and posted it on social media , hoping to find him and thank him for what he had done. It was very emotional, Dominguez said. We thought, oh, we just witnessed a miracle. Spoelstra and Baur met again at the railroad crossing Sunday. When they saw each other, they hugged. Spoelstra said she's grateful to Baur and believes things could have turned out very differently if he hadn't been there. You know, first of all, that a total stranger, would help another person, she said. I won't ever forget what he's done for me. He is a true American hero. Baur, however, doesn't describe himself that way. I’m just very fortunate that God put me right where I was, he said. "He's got a plan and we just got to follow it sometimes. We don't understand why." Witnesses say the crossing arm malfunctioned during the incident. See also: Foodborne illnesses are rising. What not to eat right now. Spoelstra says she reported the problem to Florida East Coast (FEC) Railway line and was told someone would come out to inspect the gate. The incident remains a powerful reminder of how quickly a dangerous situation at a railroad crossing can unfold and how one person's decision to act can make all the difference. For Spoelstra, there is also a personal connection that makes the story feel even more remarkable. She says her baby grandson shares the same name as the man who came to her rescue: Josiah.

hero.headline: Indian River County students head to school before sunrise as new year begins Monday
hero.body:
Indian River County public schools begin the 2026-2027 school year on Monday, with buses picking up students sometimes in the dark. High schools open their doors to students at 7:20 a.m., middle school K-8 schools at 8:10 a.m., and elementary schools at 9 a.m. Many students will be walking to bus stops in the dark on a daily basis as the days grow shorter. Students who meet the bus at the stop near State Road 60 and Rollins Ranch Road are scheduled for pickup at 5:51 a.m., according to Dr. Kyra Schafte, executive director of the school district's strategic communications and marketing.

The School District and Indian River County Sheriff's Office are urging caution regarding school bus safety throughout the year. Sheriff Eric Flowers said in a video posted on the sheriff's office Facebook page that all schools are changing and new students entering schools will go through metal detectors. He asked parents to be patient during drop off periods. Flowers said all of the safety measures will take some time for everyone to get used to.

Vehicles traveling in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped to pick up or discharge children at two-lane paved roads and at multi-lane paved roads without a raised median or physical barrier. As of May 1, Florida began issuing citations for illegal passing of a stopped school bus with stop arm extended and red lights flashing, with a $225 fine for the offense. For a second or subsequent offense within five years, the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles may suspend a driver's license for 90 days up to 6 months.

School district officials recommend children arrive at the bus stop at least 10 minutes early and stay at least 10 feet away from the roadway while waiting. Parents who drive their children to bus stops should park a safe distance away from buses during both morning pickup and afternoon drop off to help maintain clear visibility and safe loading areas. Transportation details are available on the Indian River County schools webpage at www.indianriverschools.org/o/sdirc/page/transportation, as well as the district's Facebook and Instagram accounts.

At multi-lane paved roads without a raised median or physical barrier, vehicles traveling in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped to pick up or discharge children. At two-lane paved roads, vehicles traveling in both directions must stop when a school bus is stopped to pick up or discharge children. INDIAN RIVER COUNTY – Public school for all students in Indian River County begins on Monday, Aug. High schools open their doors to students at 7:20 a.m.; middle school K-8 schools at 8:10 a.m.; and elementary schools at 9 a.m. That means many students could be walking to bus stops sometimes in the dark on a on a daily basis as the days grow shorter. That is especially true for students who meet the bus at the stop near State Road 60 and Rollins Ranch Road, scheduled for 5:51 a.m., according to Dr. Kyra Schafte, executive director of the school district’s strategic communications and marketing. “Parents who drive their children to bus stops should park a safe distance away from buses during both morning pickup and afternoon drop off to help maintain clear visibility and safe loading areas,” she said in a statement. “We also encourage families to remind students to wait until the school bus has come to a complete stop and the stop arm is fully extended before approaching or crossing the street.” Transportation details are available on the Indian River County schools webpage at www.indianriverschools.org/o/sdirc/page/transportation , as well as the district s Facebook and Instagram accounts. The School District and Indian River County Sheriff’s Office urge all parents/students/motorists to be cautious and observe rules and laws pertaining to school bus safety throughout the 2026-27 school year. “There will be new challenges with drop offs, pickups, buses,” Sheriff Eric Flowers said in a video posted on the sheriff’s office’s Facebook page. “All the schools are changing and we want to make sure your kids are safe. We’ve got measures in place to make sure that it is a smooth beginning to the school year.” “Please be patient as during drop off periods as new students entering the schools are entering through metal detectors,” he said. “All of the safety measures we have in place will take some time for everyone to get used to.” School district officials offer these tips that parents are encouraged to review with their children regarding bus safety: * Have the child arrive at the bus stop at least 10 minutes early. * Supervise younger children while they wait for the bus. * Teach children to stay well off the roadway until the bus comes to a complete stop. * Remind children to wait for the driver’s signal before crossing the street. * Ensure backpacks, clothing, and drawstrings cannot get caught in bus handrails or doors. When walking to a bus stop, children should: * Make eye contact with the driver before crossing the street * Cross at least 10 feet in front of the bus. * Never cross behind a school bus. At bus stops, students should: * Stand at least 10 feet away from the roadway while waiting. * Never play or run near traffic. * Stay out of the bus’s ‘danger zone’—the area around the front sides, and rear where the driver may not see anyone. * If something is dropped near the bus, tell the driver instead of reaching under the bus. When on the bus, students should: * Stay seated in assigned seats and wear seat belts (when equipped) while the bus is moving. * Keep hands, arms, and head inside the bus. * Keep aisles clear of backpacks and personal items. * Speak quietly so the driver can focus on driving safely. * Do not eat, drink or throw objects on the bus. * Follow the driver’s instructions at all times. “Motorists also play an important role by slowing down, remaining alert in school zones and neighborhoods, and always stopping when required by (state) law for a school bus displaying its stop arm and flashing red lights,” Schafte said. Drivers also must stop on two-lane roads and on multi-lane roads without a raised median or physical barrier, according to the state Department of Transportation’s web site As of May 1, Florida began issuing citations for illegal passing of a stopped school bus with stop arm extended and red lights flashing, with a $225 fine for the offense. For a second or subsequent offense within five years, the Department of Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles may suspend a driver’s license for 90 days up to 6 months A driver does not have to stop when traveling in the opposite direction only if the roadway is divided by a raised median, a physical barrier or an unpaved median at least five feet wide, according to the DOT web site. In addition, the driver’s cell phone must be “hands-free” in a school zone. Using a wireless communications device in a handheld manner while driving in a designated school crossing, school zone, or active work zone area is against the law, according to the DOT web site. hero.headline: Man rescues woman trapped on railroad tracks in Hobe Sound seconds before train arrives
hero.body:
Josiah Baur lifted a railroad crossing arm and pulled a trapped driver to safety seconds before a train passed through the intersection at Southeast Bridge Road and Dixie Highway in Hobe Sound on Friday evening around 5 p.m. Debbie Spoelstra was turning onto Bridge Road from Dixie Highway when a railroad crossing arm came down on top of her car, trapping her on the tracks. Her car's antenna was caught on the crossing arm.

Baur, 23, was driving home to Port Saint Lucie from work when he stopped at the crossing and saw Spoelstra's red car stuck between the gates. Dash cam video from a nearby driver captured the moment Baur ran across the tracks toward Spoelstra's car as a train approached. Baur lifted the crossing arm with both arms, allowing Spoelstra to reverse her car away from the tracks just before the train came through on her side of the tracks.

Lizzy Dominguez witnessed the rescue from her car behind Baur's vehicle at the crossing. After the rescue, Dominguez took a photo of Baur and posted it on social media to find and thank him. Spoelstra and Baur met again at the railroad crossing on Sunday and hugged when they saw each other.

Spoelstra reported the crossing arm malfunction to Florida East Coast Railway and was told someone would inspect the gate. Spoelstra plans to take Baur and his family out for dinner as a thank you. She noted that her 9-month-old grandson shares the same name as her rescuer, Josiah.
hero.article_text: Josiah Baur and Debbie Spoelstra — two strangers turned friends, brought together by an incredible act of courage.It happened last Friday around 5 p.m., when Spoelstra was driving along Southeast Bridge Road and Dixie Highway in Hobe Sound. Spoelstra made a turn, and suddenly a crossing arm came down on top of her car, trapping her on the tracks. Her car's antenna was caught on the crossing arm."I just went to turn and as soon as I turned, the gate came down on the top of my car," Spoelstra said. "Then I realized that I was trapped it was absolutely trapped.”Dash cam video obtained from a nearby driver shows the close call. As Spoelstra tried to figure out what to do, she hoped someone would come to her aid."I know for sure somebody might come up from behind and help me, but you know didn't happen and then all of a sudden I looked and I saw my guardian angel coming over the track," Spoelstra said.That's when Baur, who was on his way home from work, spotted her car. Baur was in a rush at the time and calls the moment a lesson, because he was forced to slow down and help."I looked down on my phone looked back up, and I see Miss Debbie's car stuck on the train tracks with the arm down behind it," Baur said. “As she's trying to move and I was like holy cow she's stuck in the tracks. She's going to get hit so I threw it in parking and just took off running," Baur said.As Baur ran toward her, he was tracking the approaching train. "As I was running, I was trying to see where the train was, how far off it was, how much time and also which side of the track it was on and when I noticed it was on her side of track I'm like okay now or never we gotta do this," Baur said.Baur lifted the crossing arm, allowing Spoelstra to reverse to safety — just before the train came through."It was incredible and after he had he had lifted the gate off I don't know how many seconds passed by and then the train came right by so it was a close call. It was very close," Spoelstra said.For Baur, it was a close call, but the right thing to do. "Don't hesitate to help others when they're in need. I didn't sit there and think about it, if I sat there and he hesitated who knows if I would've got there in time," Baur said. "People say she's a stranger to me but she's a child of God just like I am.”The two believe the moment was meant to be."I think it was a God thing and for those if you don't believe, I don't know it was just a miracle," said Spoelstra.Spoelstra plans to take Baur and his family out for dinner as a thank you. She also noted an interesting connection — she has a 9-month-old grandson named Josiah. She says she will never forget what Baur did."He's an amazing individual. He is my guardian angel," Spoelstra said. "I'll never forget what he's done ever. I'm truly grateful and indebted to him.”This story was reported on-air by a journalist and has been converted to this platform with the assistance of AI. hero.headline: Daytona Tortugas rally to beat St. Lucie Mets 5-4, take series at Clover Park
hero.body:
The Daytona Tortugas defeated the St. Lucie Mets 5-4 on Sunday at Clover Park, winning the seven-game series 4-3. The Tortugas scored five runs across the fourth and fifth innings to build a 5-0 lead before holding off a late Mets rally.

Mets starter Joel Lara cruised through the first three innings, allowing just one baserunner on a walk. Lara struggled in the fourth, walking the first three batters. A wild pitch brought home Ichiro Cano for the first run. Anielson Buten hit a two-run single with two outs to make it 3-0. Cano hit the first pitch from reliever Jean Brito for a two-run homer in the fifth inning that made it 5-0.

The Mets mounted a comeback in the sixth inning when Elian Pea led off with a double against Lisnerkin Lantigua, extending his hitting streak to 11 games. Kuhio Aloy ripped a two-run double with two outs to get the Mets on the board, and Simon Juan followed with an RBI single to make it 5-3. Juan added a sacrifice fly in the eighth to pull the Mets within one at 5-4.

Daytona pitchers Lantigua and Jesus Colina retired the last six Mets batters in a row to secure the win. Colina earned his first save by retiring the side in order in the ninth with a fly out and back-to-back strikeouts. The Mets fell to 16-25 in the second half and 49-58 overall. They begin a six-game commuter series at the Jupiter Hammerheads on Tuesday with first pitch at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium set for 6:30 p.m.
hero.article_text: Elian Peña started the Mets comeback bid in the sixth inning with a leadoff double against Lantigua. LUCIE – The Daytona Tortugas held off the St. Lucie Mets for a 5-4 victory in the series finale between the teams on Sunday at Clover Park. Daytona won the series 4-3. The Tortugas scored five runs across the fourth and fifth innings to take a 5-0 lead. The Mets scored three in the sixth and another run in the eighth to close the gap to one. But Daytona pitchers Lisnerkin Lantigua and Jesus Colina retired the last six Mets in a row to finish the game. Mets starter Joel Lara cruised through the first three innings, allowing just one base runner on a walk. However, Lara struggled with his command in the third, walking the first three batters. Lara threw a wild pitch that brought home Ichiro Cano for the first run. Then with two outs Anielson Buten hit a two-run single to make it 3-0. Jean Brito replaced Lara with one on and out in the fifth inning. Cano hit the first pitch from Brito for a two-run homer that made it 5-0. Meanwhile Daytona starter Justin Henschel was cruising. Henschel shut out the Mets over 5.0 innings on 75 pitches. He scattered three hits, walked one and struck out four. Elian Peña started the Mets comeback bid in the sixth inning with a leadoff double against Lantigua. The double extended Peña’s hitting streak to 11 games. Later in the inning with two outs Kuhio Aloy ripped a two-run double to get the Mets on the board. Simon Juan followed with a RBI single to make it 5-3. The first two Mets reached base to start the eighth inning vs. Lantigua but the Mets only got a sac fly by Juan to make it 5-4. Colina retired the side in order in the ninth with a fly out and back-to-back strikeouts to notch his first save. The first seven batters in the Mets order recorded a hit. Reed Stallman went 2 for 4. Julio Zayas went 1 for 3 win a single, walk and run to add to his bid for FSL Player of the Week. Austin Brown (undrafted 2025 – Chipola JC) made his team debut by pitching two scoreless innings in the seventh and eighth. The Mets (16-25, 49-58) are off on Monday. They return to action on Tuesday when they begin a six-game commuter series at the Jupiter Hammerheads. First pitch from Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium is 6:30 p.m. Your comment has been submitted.
